extracted.intended_audience: authors of the reviewed manuscript, journal editors, and researchers studying open peer review and systematic review methods
extracted.subtask_description: Peer review comments and author responses for a systematic review about Open Peer Review (OPR), focusing on definitional clarity, methods transparency, taxonomy validity, and disciplinary scope. The guidance is aimed at improving the manuscript's scope, methods, terminology, and evidence base.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clearly define the assumed purpose of peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: “you will need to more clearly define in your introduction and throughout the paper the assumed purpose of peer review” (as noted by a reviewer in relation to linking to the open final-versioning commenting portion of the discussion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State explicitly the working definition/purpose of peer review early (introduction) and maintain consistency; tie this definition to how specific OPR traits address that purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider disciplinary differences and show breakdowns
rubrics_metrics.description: Add consideration of disciplinary differences in the results and discussion; include figures showing the breakdown of OPR traits by discipline and discuss philosophical reasons for open participation and interaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a figure/table breaking down OPR trait prevalence by discipline and explicitly discuss how definitions, uptake, and meanings of OPR differ across STEM, social sciences, and humanities; acknowledge when scope precludes deeper disciplinary analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish peer review process from platform (avoid techno-determinism)
rubrics_metrics.description: Process can be decoupled from technological platforms; reviewers cautioned that some readers may conflate peer review with its technological implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make explicit the conceptual distinction between the peer review process and the platforms that host it; add textual clarifications (e.g., 'peer review can be decoupled not only from the journal, but also from any particular platform').

rubrics_metrics.name: Define 'Open Science' and bridge to social sciences & humanities
rubrics_metrics.description: Open science is not uniformly embraced across disciplines; if couching OPR under 'open science', explain the meaning and make the term inclusive of social sciences and humanities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide an explicit operational definition of 'Open Science' used in the paper and explain how it maps onto different disciplinary norms and community-based aspects (e.g., digital humanities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Present limitations and clarify methods to better scope the paper
rubrics_metrics.description: Presenting better the limitations of your method and clarifying your method will help scope the paper to be more scientifically sound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expand the methods/limitations sections to describe search strategy choices, inclusion/exclusion rules, and potential biases; be explicit about what is and is not within scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengthen conclusions; offer guidance for clarifying types of OPR
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer suggests a stronger conclusion, including perhaps a suggested guideline of clarifying what type of 'open peer review' is meant before discussing or evaluating it using the seven classifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not merely 'accept ambiguity'—recommend explicit provenance/labels for OPR variants when making evaluative claims; summarize which traits have evidence for claimed benefits and where evidence is lacking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highlight lack of evidence for efficiency claims about traits
rubrics_metrics.description: Author can strengthen the conclusion by highlighting the lack of evidence in efficiency claims about some of the seven traits mentioned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When claiming benefits (efficiency, speed, quality), indicate the strength of available evidence for each trait and point out gaps where evidence is weak or absent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-check search terms and database coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer advises double-checking terms such as 'Post-publication peer review' vs 'Open Final version commenting' and differences in results across databases (WoS vs Scopus).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Re-run and document searches (terms, databases, dates); justify term mappings used in taxonomy and report any sensitivity of results to alternative search terms/databases; correct figures if counts change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiate editorial processes from peer review processes
rubrics_metrics.description: It is worth mentioning most OPR initiatives are not directly addressing all shortcomings because one should distinguish between editorial process and peer review process; issues such as delay and expense are part of editorial process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be careful not to conflate editorial selection/acceptance, editorial workflows (delays/costs), and technical peer review (quality/soundness); when discussing 'problems with peer review', specify which sub-process is meant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meet systematic review standards and clarify scope (PRISMA compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Question whether the work meets established criteria for a systematic review; lack of clarity about the universe of literature assessed and how it was assessed; title should reflect non-systematic if appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full electronic search strategy for at least one database, list all information sources with coverage dates (PRISMA items 7 and 8), and explain any supplementary non-systematic enrichment; if non-systematic steps were used, reflect that in the title/abstract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide brief definitions when listing the seven types of openness
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘p7 – it is not helpful to list the seven types of openness without definitions. Even if the lengthy discussion follows, readers need brief definitions up front, especially for ambiguous items.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When enumerating trait types, include concise one-line definitions or a small glossary immediately to orient the reader before detailed discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider 'real-time review' as a variant or discuss dependency
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer notes 'real-time review in the open' (comments posted as ready) should be considered; author argues it depends on other traits such as open pre-review manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Either treat real-time review as an explicit trait or clearly explain how it emerges from combinations of other traits (open reports, commenting, participation, pre-review manuscript availability) and provide examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify and standardize terminology for traits (e.g., 'open pre-review manuscripts', 'open platforms')
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer questions some terminology (e.g., 'open pre-review manuscripts', 'open platforms') and suggests alternative phrasings and references (Neylon et al.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justify chosen terms, note alternative usages in the literature, and consider renaming ambiguous categories (e.g., 'open posting before formal review') while citing authorities on nomenclature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify relationship between open reports and open identities
rubrics_metrics.description: Some journals use open reports without open identities; the author should not imply that open reports always include open identities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly distinguish sub-features (open reports vs open identities) in the taxonomy and give examples of combinations (e.g., open reports + anonymized reviewers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Support empirical claims with evidence (e.g., influence of PubPeer)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer questions whether there is evidence that PubPeer has been 'a major influence'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide citations or empirical evidence for claims about the influence or impact of particular platforms or initiatives; otherwise qualify statements as conjecture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct data/figure errors and ensure internal consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer spotted a discrepancy where the author reported 22 definitions but the figure showed 23; author corrected a duplicate row.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audit tables/figures for duplicates, miscounts, and consistency with text; document corrections in errata or revised figures and note changes in author response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge that open identity review increases visibility of conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Proponents in medicine note that open identity review makes conflicts of interest more apparent and subject to scrutiny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include discussion of how open identity affects COI disclosure and scrutiny, especially in medical publishing, and provide examples or evidence where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a consistent authorial voice (singular vs 'we')
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer notes inconsistent use of singular 'I' vs royal 'we'; asks the author to decide on voice throughout the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose and apply a consistent narrative voice across the manuscript (first-person singular or plural) to improve readability and tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Map and quantify ambiguity of OPR usage to clarify discussion scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Author's response: 'quantifying the ambiguity of usage and mapping the distinct traits enables future discussion to start from a firmer basis'—i.e., explicitly map which meanings/traits are meant when using 'OPR'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a taxonomy and quantified mapping of usages/definitions (counts, examples) and explicitly state which trait combinations are being discussed in any analysis or evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: State inclusion/exclusion decisions about overlap with post-publication peer review (PPPR)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is overlap between 'open peer review' and 'post-publication peer review'; the study limits scope to items that mention 'OPR' explicitly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state inclusion/exclusion criteria concerning PPPR and other related terms; justify why articles not mentioning 'OPR' were excluded and discuss implications.
